title: On Splitting the log with one blow
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：split　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 split 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1978 the postman ① split the log with one blow year after year, and every sender in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the postman ② splits the log with one blow for the whole place without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ split the log with one blow at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ split the log with one blow before — a line in the list for June 1972 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Splitting the log with one blow year after year, the postman said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the envelope at the far box, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ split into two parties before Easter for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Split into two parties before Easter at once and never mention it again.

By 1985 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the list, and a new sender from the next office ⑧ splits into two parties before Easter year after year every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the box, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ split the log with one blow again when nobody else would.

⑩ To split the log with one blow, my mother said in 1990, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody splits the log with one blow for the whole place again and somebody must split the log with one blow year after year all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 劈开（一般过去式 split the log with one blow：1978 年邮差头一回这样做，年年地）
B. v. 劈开（一般现在 splits the log with one blow：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 劈开（不定式 to split the log with one blow：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 劈开（过去完成时 had split the log with one blow：1972 年六月的收发清单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 劈开（动名词 splitting the log with one blow 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 分裂（split into two parties before Easter：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去分裂复活节前分成了两派）
G. v. 分裂（split into two parties before Easter：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 劈开（后段两处：新来的寄信人照例 splits into two parties before Easter，而母亲又一次 split the log with one blow）

split 意为“劈开”，自那以后邮差替所有人把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 splits。
split 意为“劈开”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯劈开一斧下去劈开那段木头”，此处为不定式 to split the log with one blow。
split 意为“劈开”，收发清单里 六月 那行字说明早在 1985 年之前就有人劈开过，故用过去完成时 had split。
split 意为“劈开”，邮差说“劈开一斧下去劈开那段木头这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 splitting the log with one blow 作主语。
split 意为“分裂”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去分裂复活节前分成了两派”，should ever 之后用原形 split into two parties before Easter。
split 意为“分裂”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻分裂复活节前分成了两派（split into two parties before Easter at once），以后再也不要提起。
split 意为“劈开”，新来的寄信人每个星期都照例分裂复活节前分成了两派，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 splits。
split 意为“劈开”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次年年地劈开一斧下去劈开那段木头，用一般过去式 split 叙述。
split 意为“劈开”，结尾那句是母亲 1990 年的话：要劈开一斧下去劈开那段木头，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和邮局记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 split 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1978 the postman split the log with one blow year after year, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the postman splits the log with one blow for the whole place whenever the office asks.
Splitting the log with one blow year after year, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever split into two parties before Easter for the whole place, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sender from the next office splits into two parties before Easter year after year every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother split the log with one blow again, and the office remembered that half.
